title: Notation spec: Carcassonne tile placement
description:
Carcassonne has no standard algebraic notation. This is an invented notation for the adapter.

## Proposed notation
Tile placement + optional meeple:
  T5@3,2:R90 meeple:road
  T12@-1,0:R270
  T5@3,2 meeple:city

Components:
- T{n} = tile number/name from the tile set
- @{col},{row} = grid position
- :R{0|90|180|270} = rotation (default R0)
- meeple:{feature} = optional meeple placement on a feature (road, city, field, monastery)

## Actions
- Place tile: T5@3,2:R90
- Place tile + meeple: T5@3,2:R90 meeple:city
- Skip meeple: just the tile placement without meeple clause

## Special considerations
- Tile drawn is random (server authority) — notation records which tile was placed, not drawn
- Meeple placement is a second action within the same turn (phase-based)
- Feature identification (which road, which city) may need adjacency context

## Declarative spec
```json
{
  "notation": {
    "type": "tile_placement",
    "tile_prefix": "T",
    "position_marker": "@",
    "rotation_prefix": "R",
    "rotations": [0, 90, 180, 270],
    "meeple_keyword": "meeple",
    "features": ["road", "city", "field", "monastery"]
  }
}
```
Novel notation — may need WASM for feature disambiguation in complex board states.

## Open questions
- Is there an established Carcassonne notation in tournament play or apps?
- How to identify which specific road/city segment on a tile?
- Should we adopt the notation from BoardGameArena or another platform?
